full_judgment:
Mr. Mohammad Fazlul Karim, J:- This Petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 30.01.2008 passed by the High Court Division in First Miscellaneous Appeal No.202 of 2002 setting aside the order No.39 dated 23.04.2002 passed by the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, First Court, Chittagong in Mortgage Execution Case No.32 of 1998. 

 2. The facts of the case, in short, are that Rupali Bank Limited of 34, Dilkusha Commercial Area, Motijheel, Dhaka and one of its Branch at Chak Bazar, Chittagong obtained a decree on 24.04.1998 against the Premier Art Press, respondent No.2 and its proprietor, Ishaque Chowdhury alias Bahadur, respondent No.3, for TK.8,10,200.00 in Mortgage Suit No.72 of 1995 of the Court of Subordinate Judge and Is' Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong. Thereafter, the decree holder Bank started Execution Case No.32 of 1998 and the mortgage properties i.e. schedules I and 11 were put into auction on 02.03.2002. One Morshedul Alam became the highest bidder in respect of the property of schedule No. 1 whereas Jan-E-Alam Chowdhury, petitioner of the leave petition became the highest bidder in respect of the property of schedule No.2 and decree holder bank filed an application before the Court to accept those offers and the Bank accepted their offers and immediately, they deposited 25% of the total price and the Court directed them to deposit the remaining 75% money within 16.03.2002. Before the said date i.e. on 12.03.2002 Rupali Bank Limited, Dewan Bazar Branch, respondent No.4, filed an application to cancel the auction sale in respect of the property of schedule No.2 stating that the property in question was mortgaged with them earlier and they already obtained decree in Mortgage Suit Nos.79 and 80 of 1995 which are pending for disposal. The judgment-debtor Md. Ishaque Chowdhury also filed an application on 01.04.2002 for canceling the auction sale of the property of schedule No.2. Subsequently, on 07.04.2002 he filed an application for canceling the auction in respect of the properties of both the schedules. The decree holder Bank though filed an application on 02.03.2002 before the Court to accept the offer but subsequently, on 07.04.2002 they also filed an application for cancellation of the auction. The Execution Court rejected the applications filed by the decree holder-bank, judgment debtor and Rupali Bank, Dewan Bazar Branch, respondent No.4, on 23.04.2002 holding that there is no latches on the part of auction purchasers and since the decree holder bank and Rupali Bank, Dewan Bazar, the two branches of the same bank it is their internal matter for sharing the decretal amount and on the same day confirmed the auction sale. 

 3. Mr. A.M. Ameen Uddin, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner submitted that the decree holder Bank did not take any ground in the High Court Division that inspite of their prayer their application under Order XX rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure has not been registered as a judicial Miscellaneous case and the executing Court having decided the application on merit and having not decided on a preliminary point, the High Court Division erred in remanding the case to the executing Court in exercising its power beyond the scope of Order 41 rule 23 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate further submitted that the petitioner, being the highest bidder in respect of the property of schedule No.2 has already deposited the remaining 75% of the price and sale certificate having been issued in their favour on 19.06.2002 and they having taken delivery of possession of the property on 16.07.2002 and thus, execution case has reached to its finality and the High Court Division failed to consider that in view of the aforesaid circumstances the application under Order XXI rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed by the decree holder bank has rendered infractuous. 

 4. The High Court Division held that there is a gross illegality for not registering the petition filed by the appellant under Order XXI rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure as Miscellaneous Judicial Case as per rule 774(8) of the Civil Rules and Order and thus, the impugned order complained of is not sustainable in law. But the High Court Division found no other alternative but to send the case back on remand to the executing Court for removing the illegalities and to register the petition filed by the appellant bank under Order XXI rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure as a Miscellaneous Judicial Case and to give opportunity to the opposite party to file written objection, if any and after hearing both the parties to dispose of the same in accordance with law.
